On Location with Artichoke Dance | Robin Michals
events.location: Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club Boathouse, 165 2nd St, Brooklyn, NY, 11231, United States
events.desc: On Location with Artichoke Dance is a solo exhibition by Brooklyn-based photographer Robin Michals. Curated by Pam Wong, the exhibit showcases photographs of Artichoke Dance Company performing the Immersive Performance Tours of Gowanus conceived by Lynn Neuman in 2021, and co-hosted annually with various environmental and social justice organizations. The photographs on view feature Artichoke dancers moving through Gowanus in space and time and include images at the defunct Salt Lot in 2021 and the new 420 Carroll Street development in 2026. Michals merges the genres of dance photography and urban landscape photography in vibrant shots that capture the performances as well as the evolution of the neighborhood. The photos juxtapose the dancers as they work together to create patterns and shapes against a backdrop of the transforming waterfront. The photos offer an interpretation of the performances as a positive vision of urban life that values art, collaboration, and environmental awareness. In addition, there is a portrait of Neuman, in costume, on the tipping floor at SIMS Municipal Recycling, taken for Michals and Neuman’s collaborative project Waste Side Story. Michals and Neuman met in 2018 through a residency offered by Works on Water and Underwater New York on Governors Island. Michals, who had been working on environmental issues for 15 years, was struck by Lynn’s upcycling of plastic bags into costumes, and the pair began to work together to make images of a dancer wearing the costumes at locations that reflect the lifecycle of plastics from production to various end points including landfills and oceans. Several of these images were exhibited at The Old Stone House in 2021. Robin shifted her focus to dance photography after the pandemic, starting with her work with the Times Square Project in 2020 and 2021. For Robin, photographing the Artichoke Dance tours is an incredible opportunity to bring together her longstanding love of urban landscape photography and her much more recent, but no less profound, love of dance photography. —————- ON LOCATION WITH ARTICHOKE DANCE On view Saturdays: Sept 12, 19, 26 and Oct 3 from 1-5pm ON LOCATION WITH ARTICHOKE DANCE Programs: Sept. 12 (2:00–2:30pm): Video screening of Immersive Performance Tour Highlights: 2021–2026 with Artichoke Dance Company Sept. 12 (2:30-4:30pm): Join a guided tour using the Gowanus Augmented Reality Walking Tour App featuring animated virtual environments of the past as visual overlays on the canal-scape, as well as the Underground Waterways Soundwalk where voices from the past murmur and sing, led by Sarah Drury, Project Director. iPads and headphones provided, or download to your iPhone. The 20-minute tour will be available from 2:30-4:30pm. Sept. 19 (2:00pm): Pop-up performance by Artichoke Dance Company Sept. 26 (2:00pm): Pop-up performance by Artichoke Dance Company Sept. 26 (2:30pm): Role of the Arts in Change Making: A Conversation with Naturally Occurring Cultural Districts of New York Oct. 3 (2:00pm): Pop-up performance by Artichoke Dance Company —————- About the Artist: Robin Michals is a photographer who specializes in dance and performance. She is completely omnivorous when it comes to dance with an interest in all forms from folkloric to street dance. Her clients include the international Human Rights Arts Festival and the Queensboro Dance Festival among many others. In 2025, she had a public installation of photos of dancers at the party Vinyl Nights in Albee Square in Downtown Brooklyn, sponsored by Downtown Brooklyn Partnership. Her work has also been in numerous publications including Hyperallergic, Queens Chronicle, and Time Out. Before shifting her focus to performance, she spent 15 years documenting environment issues including climate change and the fossil fuel industries. She was raised in Manhattan and moved to Brooklyn in the last century. Robin has taught photography at City Tech, CUNY, where her students are from all over the world, for 23 years. For more info: www.robinmichals.com About Artichoke Dance: Artichoke Dance Company, based in Brooklyn, NY, is known for innovative and engaging performances paired with environmental activism, education, community building and civic engagement. Previous large-scale projects have addressed plastic pollution mitigation on Coney Island, single use plastic bags in New York, sea level rise and climate migration, the remediation of the Gowanus Canal, river revitalization in Los Angeles, and water use and rights in the desert southwest. Under the Direction of Lynn Neuman, Artichoke Dance Company also annually produces an Eco-Arts Festival during NYC Climate Week on Governors Island, bringing visual and performing arts and climate consciousness together through participatory workshops, exhibitions, and performances. Neuman began Artichoke’s Immersive Performance Tours of Gowanus drawing on her many years of experience organizing with the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for Justice. Artichoke’s ecoarts activism training program, Artichoke Ambassadors, and fellowship program, Arts Incubator for Change Making, trains and mentors the next generation of ecoarts activists. Incorporated as a non-profit in 1999, Artichoke Dance has held 23 New York seasons and toured nationally and internationally. For more info: www.artichokedance.org.

events.label: Gowanus Jug & String Band Sessions
events.location: Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club Boathouse, 165 2nd St, Brooklyn, NY, 11231, United States
events.desc: Tuesday evenings, 6-8:30 April through October. At the Gowanus Dredgers Boathouse 165 2nd Street between Bond and the Gowanus Canal. We are excited to expand our musical offerings with this new weekly jam. Dredger Host: Liz Rabson Schnore Jam Leader: Papa Ernie Vega What Jug band and String band music? Let’s start with String band music. Black String band music, which will be our focus, was created by Southern Blacks and pre-dates the Blues & Jazz. Groups which consisted of mostly stringed instruments (guitar, banjo, bass, violin, mandolin, ukulele, etc) performed a wide variety of songs and styles for all manner of social functions and for personal enjoyment; two-steps, waltzes and breakdowns for dances, ballads and love songs, humorous & novelty songs, as well as blues, jazz, and pop tunes as they came into fashion. This genre, sadly, was under-represented by the burgeoning recording industry in the 1920’s and 30’s, which helped contribute to its already declining popularity in the wake of the success of the Blues and Jazz: though groups like the Mississippi Sheiks and the Dallas String Band did make great and popular recordings. The genre never completely died out, however, and is alive and well today thanks to the perseverance of its practitioners and the dedication of its fans, which has led to a rediscovery and a new appreciation by audiences young and old. Jug band music developed in the early 20th century within Southern Black communities and was essentially a string band with a jug used as a “poor man’s tuba”, in the role of a bass instrument. Other household items as instruments were popular as well; washboard and/or spoons for percussion, washtub bass, and kazoo. These combined with the guitars, banjos, mandolins/violins of the traditional string band, along with the harmonica, made for a unique sound that won the hearts of the public in the early days of the recording industry. The Memphis Jug Band and Cannon’s Jug Stompers recorded well over a hundred examples of blues, ballads, pop and dance numbers – and they’re just the tip of the iceberg. The genre found new life in the Folk Music Revival of the 1960’s and remains popular to this day. These sessions will be open to Intermediate and above players, and we encourage you to sing along and bring a song to lead. To lead a song, you will be expected to sing it loudly enough for those around you to hear, to know the key you will sing in, and to explain the chord changes and form of the song if need be. We may also discuss some ideas for performing in an ensemble to help everyone find their place in the music. Papa Ernie Vega is a NYC singer, instrumentalist, bandleader, teacher, songwriter and performing/recording artist. He has over 20 years of professional experience and has performed at the Newport Folk Festival, the Jug Band Jubilee and the Osaka Jug Band Festival. He also taught and performed at the Port Townsend Acoustic Blues Festival from 2016-2021. He is a lover of fine cheap food, old movies, humor, and photography. More information on all the Boathouse Jams HERE

Nitehawk: Gotham Week Shorts: Fault Lines — Shorts
events.location: Nitehawk Cinema Prospect Park, 188 Prospect Park West, Brooklyn, NY, 11215
events.desc: In partnership with Nitehawk Cinema, The Gotham is proud to present its third annual Shorts-to-Features Showcase. Eight short films will be shown in their entirety for Film Lovers, Filmmakers and Industry. The slate includes shorts that have premiered at Sundance and Tribeca, including Jess McLeod’s She’s Nonbinary, executive produced by Bob Odenkirk and Jane Schoenbrun; Joel Perez’s Villa Encanto , executive produced by Lin-Manuel Miranda; and Julian Joslin’s No Longer Suitable for Use , executive produced by Sam Rockwell. After What Happened at the Library , Drama, Based on a True Story –15 mins In the wake of a terrifying encounter, an overwhelmed drag queen struggles under the weight of public attention. No Longer Suitable for Use (Project Market Title: Otherwise Innocent ), Thriller, Legal Drama – 21 mins Facing deportation that would separate him from his young son, an undocumented Syrian FBI informant, must decide how far he will go to protect his hard-earned place in the country. We are Kings , Coming of Age – 12 mins Lin and his best friend sneak into his mom’s Chinese restaurant to pirate DVDs—until his high school crush walks in, forcing him to choose between friends, family, and love. Boat People , Historical Prison Drama – 10 mins Inspired by true events, a Haitian refugee fights to survive the inhumane conditions at Guantánamo Bay. Collisions & Damages (Project Market Title: Jeremy & The Chans ), Romantic Comedy – 16 mins On the morning of her sister’s wedding, dutiful Lyall Chan spirals after catching wind of the bride and groom’s plans. Villa Encanto , Musical Drama – 16mins After her mother’s death, a teenager is uprooted from 1960s Spanish Harlem when her musician father takes a gig at a Puerto Rican summer resort in upstate New York. Through music and community, she learns to redefine the meaning of home. She’s Nonbinary , Dark Comedy/Drama – 11 mins Nonbinary Max and their straight, cis boyfriend, Jake, spiral into a cataclysmic identity crisis when Max reveals they’re off the waitlist for top surgery. We’re Not Done Yet , Drama/Comedy – 22 mins Alex visits his new single mother for a weekend at her beach house. But when he is confronted with her new independence, Alex is forced to face his own controlling nature. (2026, 123 min., DCP, Rated NR.) Film series: Shorts. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: FREE Walk-Up Paddling - 2nd St.
events.location: Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club Boathouse, 165 2nd St, Brooklyn, NY, 11231, United States
events.desc: Hop into a Gowanus Dredgers canoe and paddle at your own pace inside the protected Gowanus Canal. Enjoy discovering the canal’s unique mix of wildlife and urban waterway infrastructure, practice your paddling skills, or take a guided audio tour and learn more about the history, cleanup and revitalization of our favorite urban waterway. We’ll outfit you with a life jacket (which must be worn at all times) and paddle, offer some basic instruction on how to paddle and safety tips on how to use a canoe, and help you set off on your own self-guided journey. Trips may be limited to 20 minutes if there’s a crowd — but usually we just expect you to return to the dock 15 min. prior to closing. Who can participate? Paddling is for everyone! Free walk-up canoeing is open to all ages. Groups, families, solo paddlers, and intrepid first dates are all welcome! Minors require a guardian’s signature to participate, and all participants must sign a waiver. What should I wear? Dress for the weather: wear sunscreen, hats, and bring a water bottle — and bring layers if there’s a breeze! Close-toed shoes are recommended, and wear clothing you don’t mind potentially being splashed. Is it really free? Yes! But donations are encouraged to help us continue offering these and other programs. Can I volunteer? Yes! You can sign up to volunteer here. No prior experience is required, but we love return volunteers! Note: Volunteer shifts run from 30-minutes before the start of the program through the first two hours, or from the middle of the program to 30 minutes after the end of the scheduled time.

events.label: Cyanotype Workshop with Brian Ellis and The Gowanus Dredgers
events.location: Gowanus Dredgers Bunker (19th St.), 2 19th St., Brooklyn, NY
events.desc: Gather materials for cyanotype printmaking on a short canoe paddle in Gowanus Bay! 🎟️ RSVP REQUIRED Tickets available starting 9/22🎟️ RSVP here Join Brian Ellis and the Gowanus Dredgers for a mid-day cyanotype printmaking workshop! After a short discussion of the printmaking process, we will paddle to a nearby location to gather materials for our prints. Upon returning to the Bunker , we will set up and harvest the power of the sun to create some wonderful prints that participants will be able to take home the same day. Beyond the standard cyanotype process, we will also cover wet cyanotype, image transfer, and coffee-based bleaching and toning as time allows. Cost: Suggested donation of $5-10, however no one turned away for lack of funds. We want this to be accessible to everyone, please contact us if you have a financial hardship. RSVP Required as seats are limited. About the Artist: Brian Ellis is a process-based cyanotype artist who uses the medium to explore human physicality and detritus. Using their practice to document meaning-making in the context of waste, degradation, and impermanence, Brian’s cyanotype work utilizes wet cyanotype, singing, portraiture, interview, and print toning.

Enjoy discovering the canal’s unique mix of wildlife and urban waterway infrastructure, practice your paddling skills, or take a guided audio tour and learn more about the history, cleanup and revitalization of our favorite urban waterway. We’ll outfit you with a life jacket (which must be worn at all times) and paddle, offer some basic instruction on how to paddle and safety tips on how to use a canoe, and help you set off on your own self-guided journey. Trips may be limited to 20 minutes if there’s a crowd — but usually we just expect you to return to the dock 15 min. prior to closing. Who can participate? Paddling is for everyone! Free walk-up canoeing is open to all ages. Groups, families, solo paddlers, and intrepid first dates are all welcome! Minors require a guardian’s signature to participate, and all participants must sign a waiver. What should I wear? Dress for the weather: wear sunscreen, hats, and bring a water bottle — and bring layers if there’s a breeze! Close-toed shoes are recommended, and wear clothing you don’t mind potentially being splashed. Is it really free? Yes! But donations are encouraged to help us continue offering these and other programs. Can I volunteer? Yes! You can sign up to volunteer here. No prior experience is required, but we love return volunteers! Note: Volunteer shifts run from 30-minutes before the start of the program through the first two hours, or from the middle of the program to 30 minutes after the end of the scheduled time.

events.desc: A Persistence of Cormorants is a summer-long poetry reading series on our shoreline featuring accomplished and exceptional poets from the New York area, many of who live in Brooklyn. On each of the scheduled Sundays, from 1:30 to 3:30, up to four featured poets will read for 10 to 15 minutes each. Gerry reads poetry at the canal The readings will be followed by open mic time limited to ten readers (one poem no longer than 3 minutes) who have signed up the day of the reading on a first come basis. Reading will be outdoors at the Gowanus open shoreline and we invite you to engage with the emerging Gowanus Canal habitat as we witness the EPA conduct their SuperFUN/d cleanup program. Participation is free but we encourage donations to sustain the efforts of the Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club, an advocacy stewardship organization who has been representing neighborhood interests for over two decades. events.label: Gowanus Jug & String Band Sessions
events.location: Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club Boathouse, 165 2nd St, Brooklyn, NY, 11231, United States
events.desc: Tuesday evenings, 6-8:30 April through October. At the Gowanus Dredgers Boathouse 165 2nd Street between Bond and the Gowanus Canal. We are excited to expand our musical offerings with this new weekly jam. Dredger Host: Liz Rabson Schnore Jam Leader: Papa Ernie Vega What Jug band and String band music? Let’s start with String band music. Black String band music, which will be our focus, was created by Southern Blacks and pre-dates the Blues & Jazz. Groups which consisted of mostly stringed instruments (guitar, banjo, bass, violin, mandolin, ukulele, etc) performed a wide variety of songs and styles for all manner of social functions and for personal enjoyment; two-steps, waltzes and breakdowns for dances, ballads and love songs, humorous & novelty songs, as well as blues, jazz, and pop tunes as they came into fashion. This genre, sadly, was under-represented by the burgeoning recording industry in the 1920’s and 30’s, which helped contribute to its already declining popularity in the wake of the success of the Blues and Jazz: though groups like the Mississippi Sheiks and the Dallas String Band did make great and popular recordings. The genre never completely died out, however, and is alive and well today thanks to the perseverance of its practitioners and the dedication of its fans, which has led to a rediscovery and a new appreciation by audiences young and old. Jug band music developed in the early 20th century within Southern Black communities and was essentially a string band with a jug used as a “poor man’s tuba”, in the role of a bass instrument. Other household items as instruments were popular as well; washboard and/or spoons for percussion, washtub bass, and kazoo. These combined with the guitars, banjos, mandolins/violins of the traditional string band, along with the harmonica, made for a unique sound that won the hearts of the public in the early days of the recording industry. The Memphis Jug Band and Cannon’s Jug Stompers recorded well over a hundred examples of blues, ballads, pop and dance numbers – and they’re just the tip of the iceberg. The genre found new life in the Folk Music Revival of the 1960’s and remains popular to this day. These sessions will be open to Intermediate and above players, and we encourage you to sing along and bring a song to lead. To lead a song, you will be expected to sing it loudly enough for those around you to hear, to know the key you will sing in, and to explain the chord changes and form of the song if need be. We may also discuss some ideas for performing in an ensemble to help everyone find their place in the music. Papa Ernie Vega is a NYC singer, instrumentalist, bandleader, teacher, songwriter and performing/recording artist. He has over 20 years of professional experience and has performed at the Newport Folk Festival, the Jug Band Jubilee and the Osaka Jug Band Festival. He also taught and performed at the Port Townsend Acoustic Blues Festival from 2016-2021. He is a lover of fine cheap food, old movies, humor, and photography. More information on all the Boathouse Jams HERE

events.label: Full Moon Gowanus Voyage - OCTOBER
events.location: Gowanus Dredgers Bunker (19th St.), 2 19th St., Brooklyn, NY
events.desc: Join our Crew on a full-moon guided adventure!! Meet at the the Gowanus Dredgers Bunker, at the end of 19th St / off 3rd Ave, 11232 – NOT our 2nd St. boathouse. 🎟️ Tickets required, get yours here. 🎟️ (Tickets go on sale Thursday, October 1 at 12:00 PM) Moonrise 17:58 |Sunset 18:01 | Civil End 18:29 | Nautical End 19:00 The stars should be on display along with harbor lights. We will provide lights for each canoe, you’re welcome to bring/wear your own head lamp as well. Each canoe will have up to 3 people. Solo paddlers are welcome, you will be paired with other members of the group based on experience and comfort in a canoe. Close-toed shoes are recommended, and wear clothing you don’t mind potentially being splashed. Use a restroom before arrival, as we have limited facilities on-site. Due to EPA cleaning of the Gowanus Canal, voyage will head towards the 9th St bridge and return to Gowanus Bay and our new South Gowanus Bunker. If raining or threatening weather (high winds, lightning) by 3:30 pm we may cancel. Attendees will be notified via the email used to purchase tickets. Tour is not cancelled due to clouds but let’s hope for a clear sky for the moon rise! Tickets are nonrefundable for any event that proceeds as planned. We will offer the option to transfer your ticket to another event if we have to cancel for weather. Transfer must be requested before the tour starts. If you choose not to transfer, the cost of your ticket becomes a tax-deductible donation to the Gowanus Dredgers.

events.label: Brooklyn Folk Festival: Banjo Toss Competition
events.location: Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club Boathouse, 165 2nd St, Brooklyn, NY, 11231, United States
events.desc: Each year, as part of the Brooklyn Folk Festival , contestants gather on the banks of the fetid Gowanus Canal to see who can throw a banjo the farthest in the – BANJO TOSS: BANJO THROWING COMPETITION! The special “throwing banjo”, attached to a rope is tossed into the canal, a federally designate Super Fund site. The marked rope pays out, showing how far the banjo has been tossed. It is then hauled back in for the next throw. The Brooklyn Folk Festival is presented each year by the Jalopy Theatre & School of Music, a grassroots Red Hook, Brooklyn community space that is a music venue, music school, and record label. We are excited to support the Banjo Toss event activity so please stop by and join the fun! We are told the best preparation for this competition is to attend a show at the Brooklyn Folk Festival so purchase tickets now before they are sold out. While bearded men and women are growing in popularity as more people live, work and play in our Gowanus neighborhood, we are assured by the organizers that beards are optional. Our amazing collection of competitors reinforces the Dredgers theme of inclusion so stop by to cheer our competitors or compete in the toss as well!

events.label: Yom Kippur School Holiday in Prospect Park
events.desc: Join Prospect Park Alliance for family friendly programming on the school holiday for Yom Kippur. Nature Exploration Prospect Park Audubon Center, 10 am–3 pm Nature Around Us, 10 am–3 pm: Enjoy different seasonal discovery stations and nature themed activities that will introduce you to the plants, insects and animals that call the park home. The Lake and Lullwater are home to many plants and animals. Help us to test the water quality and investigate pond samples that are filled with living organisms. Fall Leaf Discovery, 2–3 pm: Join us as we delve into the wonder of nature! Are you curious about why and when trees shed their leaves? Gain hands-on experience in citizen science as we explore the Prospect Park environment and witness how changing temperatures affect the trees. We will provide you with a guide to help you record your observations. This program leaves the Audubon Center promptly at 2 pm. ReImagine Lefferts Open Hours, 12–5 pm Lefferts Historic House, Free Visit the Lefferts Historic House for family friendly outdoor and indoor exhibits, activities, workshops and special programs that explore the legacies of resistance and resilience of the Indigenous peoples of Lenapehoking, whose unceded lands the park and house rests upon, and the Africans enslaved by the Lefferts family. Carousel Rides, 12–5 pm Children’s Corner, $3 per ride; $13 for a book of 5 tickets; Unlimited with Prospect Park Alliance Family Supporter membership Make the most of the Yom Kippur school holiday at the park’s beloved Carousel. Join the Alliance at the Family Supporter level or above, and your family (up to 4 people) will receive unlimited rides on the Carousel for a full year!

events.location: Old Stone House, 336 3rd Street, Brooklyn, NY, 11215
events.desc: A site-specific history of botany as a tool for European expansion in North America and the pervasive legacies of colonialism in environmental studies today. $25. Contact angelmartinezlombardo@gmail.com for sliding scale options.

events.desc: Children’s Corner, $3 per ride, $13 for a book of 5 tickets, Free with Prospect Park Alliance Family Supporter membership or higher. Enjoy a ride on Prospect Park’s beloved 1912 Carousel. Open Thursdays – Sundays and Holidays, this treasured historic attraction features magnificent carved horses, lions, giraffes and deer. Join the Alliance at the Family Supporter level or above and enjoy unlimited free rides!

events.label: Molière in the Park: Don Juan
events.desc: Join Molière in the Park, in partnership with Prospect Park Alliance, for a free production of Molière’s most subversive masterpiece, Don Juan. Following the infamous seducer over a single day of defiance and betrayal, this thrilling production blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural. Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, featuring live original cello music by Drama Desk nominee Johnathan Moore. RSVP About Molière in the Park: The mission of Molière in the Park (MIP) is to foster empathy and unity within the diverse communities in Brooklyn through the arts. We offer free opportunities for all to come together in Prospect Park and beyond and experience the benefits of theater. MIP’s vision is of a Brooklyn where all communities can benefit equally from access to theater and the Arts. Find out more at www.moliereinthepark.org
